title: The El Segundo week in interactives: sunsets, LAX at night, hardware row and pizza
dek: Four new interactive editions on elsegundo.xyz, each with something to turn or tap, plus a museum room of 111 public-domain works. Not an official City site.
author: cc
source: Claude (cc) for Michael Hoydich, 8 November 2026. Directive in the Claude Duet project chat, 03:25 UTC: "build out a pointcast feature or two about elsegubdodotxyz". Facts from the linked elsegundo.xyz pages, each loaded HTTP 200 at about 03:35 UTC on 8 November 2026. elsegundo.xyz is independent and is not an official City of El Segundo site.
body:
elsegundo.xyz is Michael Hoydich's independent local commons for El Segundo and the 25 miles around it. It is not an official City of El Segundo site. Between November 7 and 8 it published four interactive editions, each with something to turn, tap or cut, and each sourced line by line. Here they are, with the one number from each worth knowing.

Where the sun goes down. A sunset compass for five South Bay beaches. Pick a beach and a day, and it draws where the sun meets the horizon: open ocean in December, the Channel Islands around the equinoxes, and in summer behind the Malibu coast. From El Segundo Beach the sunset point swings about 57 degrees over a year, and from about April 21 to August 20 the sun sets behind land. From Redondo Beach Pier that window is only about 70 days. Computed in your browser from NOAA's solar equations; estimates, not observations.

LAX after midnight. A clock of the night rules Los Angeles World Airports publishes, as heard from the fence line. From midnight to 6:30 a.m., Over-Ocean Operations flip the traffic pattern out to sea. From 10 p.m. the inner runways take priority. Pick a Santa Ana wind and the whole airport turns around. LAX handled 580,996 landings and takeoffs in 2025. The clock shows what the rules say should happen, not what the tower is doing tonight, and the page is not affiliated with LAWA or the FAA.

Hardware row. A filterable map of 19 hard tech companies within about 17 miles of City Hall: reentry capsules, a portable nuclear microreactor, bus-sized satellites, rockets, radars and factories that run themselves. Six of them sit within about 3 miles. Vast in Long Beach now targets 2027 for Haven-1, a commercial space station. Every description is quoted from the company's own site, nobody paid to be listed, and some of these companies make weapons.

The business of pizza. A case study that starts in Naples and ends on Main Street. U.S. pizza restaurants were projected at $49.6 billion in 2025 across 75,736 pizzerias, more than half of them independent. You can cut a pie into its costs yourself, see why cheese and labor rule the sheet, and work out what a soft serve add-on does. A companion guide covers EZPZ, the pizza and soft serve shop at 321 Main Street, and what critics have written since it opened this summer.

The art on the walls

Every edition is illustrated with public-domain paintings, not stock photos or AI images: Frederic Edwin Church over the sunset compass, Martin Johnson Heade over the night airport. They come from the site's new museum room, 111 public-domain works from four museums' open-access collections, picked for a town between the airport and the sea. Each one is credited and links to the museum's own record.

Why PointCast is carrying these

PointCast and elsegundo.xyz are neighbors. PointCast is the broadcast, and elsegundo.xyz is the local guide it points at. All four editions were written by Claude with Claude research helpers at Michael Hoydich's request, and each says so on the page. The canonical versions live on elsegundo.xyz.

Written by Claude (cc). Facts come from the linked elsegundo.xyz pages; nothing here is original reporting.
